Repair and extend the eMicro CPU control-plane project in `/workspace/project`.
The supplied multi-file system uses a real FAdo compiler, state exporter and map loader.
Make the pipeline compile policies into canonical live-state images and replay causal events.
Implement atomic image publication, pinned versions and exact resource accounting.
Support multiplexed requests, cloned process identities, transport and file-mediated handoffs.
The complete schema, language, boundaries and output semantics are in `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
This is an offline userspace abstraction; kernel attachment and service deployment are excluded.
The whole `/workspace/project` directory is the deliverable; additional ordinary files are allowed.
Keep `driver.py` as the JSON entry point; internal implementation choices are yours.
`python3 /workspace/launch.py` reads one request from stdin and writes one response to stdout.
Use only the supplied Python 3.11 runtime, standard library and pinned offline dependencies.
Do not install packages or require network access, threads, subprocesses or external services.
Verification executes the collected project read-only as a nonroot user with fresh state.
Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable; 2 GiB memory and 256 MiB stdout limits are public.
The two-minute CPU budget applies to the entire maximum batch, including compilation and replay.
Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py` as the image's nonroot user for a small CLI sanity check.
The starter is incomplete; passing the public sanity check does not cover the full contract.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The eMicro CPU control-plane project in `/workspace/project` is repaired and complete.

**What was fixed and added**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `driver.py` | JSON entry point: bounded stdin read, envelope/job validation, **streamed** response (4 MiB buffer), exit 0 always |
| `envelope.py` | strict JSON text rules: BOM, 64 container levels (memory-safe structural scan), duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, 4300-digit ints, 24 MiB input, ≤4 jobs |
| `validate.py` | event schema per op, registry/limit static bounds, whole-request budgets (200000 events, 16 stages, 8 MiB policy bytes, 32768 atoms, 65536 path services) counted over structurally valid jobs only |
| `syntax.py` | context-aware policy scanner + parser (Lark-LALR lexer parity, empty paths, keyword names, exact whitespace set) and every per-string bound |
| `compiler/automata.py` | canonical images: match-trie + KMP residuals → joint product → Moore refinement (monotone block count enables early row rejection) → dead-residual removal, BFS labelling, row/cell census; empty language now yields all-`DENY` instead of raising |
| `compiler/compiler.py` | real FAdo oracle (epsilon NFAs, FAdo subset construction/Brzozowski minimisation) sharing the canonical writer; `EMICRO_VERIFY=1` cross-checks every stage |
| `ebpf/create_dfa.py` | state exporter with label-ordered columns and registry check |
| `ebpf/helper.py` | `MemoryMap` + full lifecycle `Agent`: atomic publication/retirement, epoch/stream/request/generation high-water marks, pinned-epoch advances, cloned identities, `EMC4` wire transport with idempotent retransmission, file-mediated store/load handoffs, exact per-context/per-packet/per-file references, `inspect` census — every rejection changes nothing |
| `selftest.py` | 111 in-process contract checks |

**Verification performed:** `public_check.py` passes; differential fuzzing (≈10k rounds) of the fast engine vs FAdo vs a brute-force language oracle; replay fuzzing vs an independently transcribed model with cold-recount invariants; multi-job end-to-end CLI batches; parser parity plus a bound-breach audit against a Lark reference; boundary suites for u32 exhaustion, capacities, surrogate/BOM/nesting/total rules. Maximum-shaped batches run in ~4–11 CPU seconds with ~120 MB RSS and a 106 MB streamed response, well inside the 120 s / 2 GiB / 256 MiB windows.

echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
